answer: An agent economy can require every account to lock a scarce token deposit before it may submit work, then slash that deposit when independent audits prove fraud or duplicate identities. The deposit is not proof that an agent is human; it makes identities costly to multiply, while slashing ties the cost to detected abuse. An attacker must fund each Sybil account and risk losing its stake, so flooding the river of tasks with disposable agents becomes expensive. A pigment-based label or a bridge between accounts alone would not provide this deterrent.
